title: Direct connection: a world from an unlisted client needs your consent
covers: Allow unlisted clients and the Allow this world consent dialog on the seat card
context: A client that is not in the registry may bring its own world. The host reads who sent it, sees a check result and must allow it before it runs. The dialog focuses Refuse first.
changed: views/LobbyMembers: Review the world of, the consent dialog

setup.label: launch
setup.text: The bundle-4 launch above. If the welcome tour opens by itself, press Skip.

setup.label: world
setup.text: One small world of the tab Archipelago index installed (Library, Games, Add). Pick one without Python packages. Not Relic of the Past and not Chrono Trigger.

setup.label: session
setup.text: The session Direct check of the previous test, with Allow direct connections, Host approval and Allow unlisted clients on, one player of your own and a ready engine.

steps: Close the tab of the last test (it asks to stop the room if it still hosts; confirm). Open Sessions, pick Direct check and press Run. The tab opens in the Lobby phase.
Copy the session code from the stage header and the Lobby address from the Network widget.
Open Sessions, Join a session, paste both, press Look at the session, and set Game to your world. Set Options to Game defaults, a Player name such as Guest2 and a Your name. Press Join as a player.
Back in the tab press Approve followed by the name you typed for Your name.
The card shows Needs your consent and a button Review the world of Guest2 appears.
Press Review the world of Guest2. A dialog titled Allow this world? opens. It says the world was not published by a listed client and lists Game, World version, Size, Hash, Sent by, Client and Check.
The focus starts on Refuse, not on Allow this world. Press Allow this world. The slot changes to Ready.
Press Run in the tab. Both your player and Guest2 get a file in the live room.
pass: The slot waits with Needs your consent and the dialog shows the world details and the check result.
Refuse is focused first, and Allow this world makes the slot Ready.
Run makes a seed that includes the unlisted world.
fail: The world runs without any question.
The dialog is missing details, or it focuses Allow this world.
After Allow the slot stays blocked, or Run fails because of the world.
notes: Not every index world generates on every engine. If Run fails after the consent worked, note the sentence shown and mark the consent part as passed.
Refuse can be tried on a second join: the slot shows Refused and the player cannot run.
A world that needs Python packages asks for package consent when you add it, before this test. Pick a world without packages.
